column3: Hebrew expressly says “there” and “also” before describing the weeping; BSB leaves these words unexpressed.
Hebrew says “in her midst,” referring to Babylon; BSB has only “there.”
Hebrew requests “words of a song” and “joy”; BSB makes the latter “songs of joy.”
Hebrew says “may my right hand forget,” without an expressed object; BSB interprets this as “cease to function.”
Hebrew retains the image “above the head of my joy”; BSB renders it “as my greatest joy.”
Hebrew says “the day of Jerusalem,” without “fell,” and repeats the same command, “Lay bare, lay bare.”
Hebrew describes Babylon as “devastated”; BSB has “doomed to destruction.” It repeats the language of repayment.
Hebrew has “the rock” in the singular; BSB has “the rocks.”
